channel.title: Field Notes
channel.description: A demo publication for Hunch. Every article here is fictional.

item.title: Keeping a sourdough starter alive through the summer
item.description: Warm kitchens make wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria run fast. Feed your starter more often, use cooler water, and keep a dried backup in the cupboard so a hot week never ends your bread baking.

item.title: Reading the air of planets around other stars
item.description: When an exoplanet passes in front of its star, starlight filters through its atmosphere. Space telescopes split that light into spectra that reveal water vapour, carbon dioxide and methane.

item.title: Compiling Rust to WebAssembly for the browser
item.description: With wasm-bindgen and a small build step, Rust code runs in the browser at near-native speed. We port an image filter and compare it with plain JavaScript.

item.title: Crossing the Alps by night train
item.description: A sleeper train leaves Zurich after dinner and arrives in Vienna for breakfast. We compare couchettes and private cabins and what to pack for a comfortable night on the rails.

item.title: Shaping baguettes without a couche
item.description: A rolled kitchen towel dusted with rice flour holds the dough's shape just as well as a linen couche. We walk through pre-shaping, the final roll and scoring the loaves before they go into a steamy oven.

item.title: Why dark sky reserves matter for astronomy
item.description: Light pollution hides the Milky Way from most people on Earth. Dark sky reserves limit outdoor lighting so astronomers and stargazers can still see faint galaxies and meteor showers.

item.title: Web components that render on the server first
item.description: Declarative shadow DOM lets a custom element arrive fully rendered in the HTML. The JavaScript only upgrades it, so the page shows content before any script runs.

item.title: Eating your way through Lisbon
item.description: Custard tarts warm from the oven, grilled sardines and tiny neighbourhood tascas. A walking route through Lisbon's old quarters, planned around the best food stops.

item.title: Fresh egg pasta with only a fork and a rolling pin
item.description: Semolina, eggs and a pinch of salt become silky tagliatelle. Knead until the dough is smooth, rest it under a bowl, then roll it thin enough to read a newspaper through.

item.title: What happens inside a coral during a marine heatwave
item.description: Corals expel the symbiotic algae that feed them when ocean water stays too warm. Reefs can recover if the heat passes quickly, but repeated bleaching events leave them starving.

item.title: Running machine learning models on the device
item.description: Small quantized models now run in the browser and on phones. On-device inference keeps personal data local, works offline and avoids server costs.

item.title: Driving Iceland's ring road in winter
item.description: Short days, icy roads and the chance of northern lights. How to plan a winter road trip around Iceland, from rental cars to weather apps and glacier hikes.

item.title: Cold brew coffee at home, and why grind size matters
item.description: Steeping coarse ground coffee in cold water for sixteen hours gives a sweet, low-acid concentrate. Grind too fine and the brew turns muddy and bitter; filter twice for a clean cup.

item.title: Life without sunlight at deep sea hydrothermal vents
item.description: Microbes at hot vents on the ocean floor turn hydrogen sulfide into energy. Tube worms, shrimp and crabs build whole ecosystems on that chemistry, far from any sunlight.

item.title: Stopping layout shift with modern CSS
item.description: Reserve space with aspect-ratio, size-adjusted fallback fonts and fixed slots for late content. Cumulative layout shift drops to zero and pages stop jumping under the reader's thumb.

item.title: Kyoto's quiet temples away from the crowds
item.description: Skip the busiest shrines at noon and visit moss gardens and mountain temples early in the morning, when the paths are empty and the light is soft.

item.title: A fermented chili hot sauce for beginners
item.description: Salt brine, garlic and fresh chilies sit in a jar for two weeks while lactic acid fermentation builds a deep, tangy heat. Blend, strain and bottle; it keeps for months in the fridge.

item.title: Gene editing crops to survive drought
item.description: CRISPR lets plant geneticists switch off single genes that make wheat and rice lose water. Field trials show edited crops holding their yield through dry seasons.

item.title: Website analytics without tracking visitors
item.description: Aggregate counts, no cookies and no cross-site identifiers can still tell you which pages people read. We compare privacy-preserving analytics tools and what they give up.

item.title: Seeing Europe by rail on a budget
item.description: Rail passes, regional trains and booking early keep costs down. A three-week route connects Amsterdam, Berlin, Prague, Vienna and Venice without a single flight.

item.title: Five winter soups built on one vegetable stock
item.description: Roast onions, carrots and celery, simmer them with herbs, and you have the base for lentil, barley, potato-leek, mushroom and white bean soups all season long.

item.title: The chemistry of roasting coffee beans
item.description: Inside a roaster, Maillard reactions and caramelization create hundreds of aroma compounds. Light roasts keep more acidity and fruit; dark roasts trade them for bitterness and body.

item.title: SQLite is everywhere, including your browser
item.description: SQLite compiled to WebAssembly with the origin private file system gives web apps a real relational database that persists locally and works offline.

item.title: Hut-to-hut hiking in the Dolomites
item.description: The Alta Via trails link mountain huts with hearty dinners and dormitory beds. Plan a week of hiking among limestone peaks, with tips on booking huts and packing light.

item.title: Knife skills that make weeknight cooking faster
item.description: Hold the blade with a pinch grip, curl your guiding fingers, and let the knife rock. Dicing onions, julienning carrots and mincing herbs become quick and safe.

item.title: Measuring glacier retreat with satellites and old photographs
item.description: Comparing satellite images with century-old expedition photographs shows how far alpine glaciers have retreated as the climate warms, and how fast meltwater is rising.

item.title: Vector search explained with embeddings
item.description: An embedding model turns text into vectors so that similar meanings sit close together. Cosine similarity and approximate nearest neighbour indexes find related documents fast.

item.title: A night of street food in Bangkok
item.description: Boat noodles, grilled pork skewers and mango sticky rice. Where to find Bangkok's best night markets and how to order when you do not speak Thai.

item.title: Dense, dark rye bread the Nordic way
item.description: Rye flour has little gluten, so the loaf relies on a sour starter, cracked grains and a long, slow bake in a tin. Wait a full day before slicing for the best crumb.

item.title: A field guide to this year's meteor showers
item.description: The Perseids, Geminids and Quadrantids peak on predictable nights. Find a dark site away from city lights, let your eyes adapt for twenty minutes and look up.

item.title: Building a quiet mechanical keyboard
item.description: Lubed linear switches, foam dampening and a gasket-mounted plate turn a clacky keyboard into a soft, quiet one that still feels great to type on.

item.title: Stargazing in the Atacama desert
item.description: The driest desert on Earth has some of the clearest skies anywhere. Observatories and dark sky tours let travellers see the Milky Way and distant galaxies with their own eyes.
